sources.entry: pyodbc - An ODBC bridge for connecting to SQL Server and any other ODBC-accessible database.

summary.one_liner: pyodbc is a Python module that gives simple access to ODBC-accessible databases, implementing the DB API 2.0 specification.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes pyodbc as an open source Python module for accessing ODBC databases, implementing the DB API 2.0 specification with additional Pythonic conveniences. It is installed with pip, and the README says precompiled binary wheels are provided for multiple Python versions on most Windows, macOS, and Linux platforms. On other platforms it is built from source, which requires a C++ compiler. On macOS and Unix, the README advises installing an ODBC driver manager such as unixODBC first; on Windows the driver manager is built in. The README itself is short and points to external docs for platform setup and usage, plus release notes.
use_cases: query any ODBC-accessible database from Python
run DB API 2.0 SQL queries from Python code
access databases through an ODBC driver manager
how_to_run: brew install unixodbc (macOS, optional if no ODBC driver manager is installed)
stack: ODBC driver manager (unixODBC on macOS/Unix, built into Windows)
notable: Implements the Python DB API 2.0 specification
Connects to SQL Server and any other ODBC-accessible database
Precompiled wheels for most Windows, macOS, and Linux platforms
Driver manager is built into Windows
caveats: On other platforms, pyodbc builds from source and needs a suitable C++ compiler
On macOS and Unix, an ODBC driver manager must be installed separately
README is brief and defers setup details to external documentation
keywords: connect to sql server from python
